fields.features_heading: What a Clinic Hands Off to Software First
fields.features_subheading: Healthcare automation is software running the repeat steps of the front desk and billing, so staff keep the work that needs a person.
fields.feature_1:
Rules written as plain sentences

Describe each automation the way you would brief a new hire, such as who is offered a slot that opens. Emergent builds the app and its logic, and a prompt changes a rule.
fields.feature_2:
Connects to the systems you already run

Any system with an API can send data into the app or receive its updates. The scheduling and billing software the practice runs today stays in place, and the app works beside it.
fields.feature_3:
Faxes and scans read into fields

Upload a faxed form or a scanned insurance card, and AI reads it into structured fields. A value the AI is unsure of goes to a person to confirm before the record is saved.
fields.feature_4:
Every delay has one named owner

An overdue item goes to a named person in Slack, by email, or in the app, and a reminder follows if nobody acts. You pick who hears about each delay as you write the rule.
fields.feature_5:
Records kept in a database you own

Appointments and referrals are stored in a database you own, and each approval is logged with the name of the person who gave it. Pull a report whenever you need one.
fields.feature_6:
The code is yours on paid plans

Export the full code of the app to your GitHub repository on paid plans. An IT team or an outside developer can read every rule before the app touches a patient record.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Clinic Automations Worth Running First
fields.tab_content_1:
One tap on Reschedule refills a Thursday slot

Vesna Kjellberg has a Thursday 9:30 a.m. visit at Cedarbrook Family Medicine, and the app emails her a reminder 2 days ahead. She taps Reschedule and moves to Friday at 2:15 p.m. The app then emails the open Thursday slot to Benedek Szabados, first on the waitlist, and holds it for him.
fields.tab_content_2:
A faxed referral, read into the right fields

A faxed referral for Thandiwe Mabuza arrives from Dr. Kasongo Ilunga. The app reads the referring doctor, the reason, her date of birth, and her member ID into a new record. The smudged member ID reads at low confidence, and the record waits for Ifeoma Fairweather at the front desk to check that one field.
fields.tab_content_3:
Five business days of silence reaches billing

Request PA-3318 for Gunnhild Ferreira-Lowe's knee MRI goes to her insurer on a Monday. Each request gets 5 business days for an answer. With no answer by the next Monday, the app marks PA-3318 overdue and sends Dashiell Pellegrini, the billing coordinator, a direct message in Slack with a Call insurer button.
fields.tab_content_4:
Glove orders over $500 wait for the practice manager

The exam glove count in the supply room drops to 12 boxes, under the reorder point of 20. The app drafts a reorder of 40 boxes at $16 each, $640 in all. Orders over $500 go to Abebe Sundqvist, the practice manager, who approves this one in the app, and the log records his name next to the decision.

fields.howto_title: How to Automate Your Clinic's Front Office
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to plan healthcare automation around the tasks your front desk repeats, then build and test it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 List what the front desk repeats
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Write each rule as a sentence
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Decide what a person must approve
fields.howto_step_1_des: Keep a tally at the front desk for one normal week and write down every task done more than 10 times. Mark the ones that follow a fixed rule, such as reminder calls or typing up referrals. Start with those.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Write the rules as plain instructions: send new-patient forms 3 days before the first visit, and flag a referral nobody has booked within 7 days. Emergent builds the app, its database, and the logic from those sentences.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Connect the scheduling and billing systems through their APIs. Each automation should read from the system that owns the fact: appointment times from the schedule, claim status from billing.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Mark every action that spends money or changes a patient's record. Each of those waits for a named approver, who sees the source document next to the Approve button and decides there.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Agree on what data the app may read
fields.howto_step_5_des: Ask whoever owns privacy at the practice which records the app may read and who may see each screen. Begin with the automations that need the least patient detail, such as supply counts.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Run two weeks of past appointments and referrals through the app before it contacts a patient. Check every reminder time and every routed referral. Fix a rule by prompting, then run the same two weeks again.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Switch on one automation at a time
fields.howto_step_7_des: Start with supply reorders, since they never reach a patient. Watch two weeks of live use and read every item a person had to correct. Then switch on the next automation.

faq_plan.a: Automation in healthcare, or healthcare automation, is software handling the administrative and clinical workflows that would otherwise need manual work, such as claims processing and eligibility checks. At a clinic, the front desk is the place to start. Keep every decision about a patient's care with a clinician, and automate the paperwork around it.

faq_plan.q: How do I set up healthcare automation?
faq_plan.a: Start with one task that follows a fixed rule and describe it in a prompt to Emergent's AI automation builder, which turns it into a working app. Link the app to the system that holds the data, run it against past appointments, and switch it on once every result checks out.

faq_plan.q: What are some examples of healthcare automation companies?
faq_plan.ref: What are some examples of healthcare automation companies?

prov.original: What are some examples of healthcare automation companies?

faq_plan.a: UiPath is one: its healthcare platform integrates with Epic, Cerner, Meditech, and payer systems without replacing them. Automation Anywhere is another, orchestrating AI agents across provider and payer workflows. SS&C Blue Prism sells an enterprise AI-powered platform built for healthcare workflow automation and orchestration.

faq_plan.q: What do healthcare automation solutions cover?
faq_plan.a: Healthcare automation solutions cover administrative workflows, such as scheduling, referrals, and claims, as well as clinical workflows that touch care itself. Both sides lean on document automation wherever referrals or insurance cards arrive as faxes and scans.

faq_plan.q: What should healthcare workflow automation take on first?
faq_plan.a: Healthcare workflow automation should take on tasks that follow a fixed rule and change no clinical decision, such as visit reminders, waitlist offers, referral data entry, and supply reorders. Leave diagnosis and treatment choices with clinicians. On Emergent there is no task cap, so a busy reminder schedule keeps running through a heavy month.

faq_plan.q: Is clinical workflow automation different from front-office automation?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Clinical workflow automation touches care itself, such as routing a lab result to the clinician who ordered it, while front-office automation handles the paperwork around a visit. Put a clinician's sign-off on any step that changes care, and start on the front-office side, where a mistake costs a phone call rather than a patient's safety.

faq_plan.q: What should I look for in healthcare workflow automation software?
faq_plan.a: Look for software that reads from your existing scheduling and billing tools, sends uncertain data to a person, logs who approved what, and lets you change a rule without a developer. The approval step works like a content approval workflow: a named reviewer decides, and the record keeps the decision.

faq_plan.q: Can a small practice run clinic workflow automation without a developer?
faq_plan.a: Yes. A small practice can start clinic workflow automation with tasks that need only a calendar and email, such as visit reminders and waitlist offers. Emergent builds the app from a plain-English prompt, and the free tier covers building and publishing. Bring in someone technical when it is time to connect the scheduling or billing system.

faq_plan.q: How does healthcare automation connect to a clinic's patient records system?
faq_plan.ref: which integration middleware supports healthcare automation
flagged: PA6 asker unclear: fragment or name (no question word)
faq_plan.a: Through each system's API, or through FHIR, a standard for exchanging healthcare information electronically. Ask the company behind your records system whether its API allows writes or only reads. That decides whether the app can book a slot or only see one. Emergent apps connect to any tool with an API, syncing data in and out.

faq_plan.q: Can healthcare automation handle the bills a practice pays?
faq_plan.ref: which healthcare automation platform has most integrations
faq_plan.a: Yes. A practice's bills follow the same steps as accounts payable automation in any business. The app reads each bill into structured fields, sends any field it cannot read with confidence to a person, and posts the rest. Start with recurring bills, such as lab services and equipment leases, where the amount barely changes.
